summary:
We developed PyroSage, a microgravity fire intelligence platform featuring "Fiction Combustion"—an interactive 3D pre-flight simulator powered by 77 NASA-grounded combustion analysis techniques.

In space, fire lacks buoyancy, forming spherical mantles and invisible "cool flames" that evade terrestrial smoke detectors. PyroSage addresses this by letting researchers control gravity, oxygen, pressure, and fuel flow to predict flame morphology, soot formation, and extinction limits in real time. It pairs multimodal experiment uploads directly against verified NASA flight records (FLEX, BASS-II).

With spaceflight fire tests costing millions, PyroSage provides an essential, risk-free sandbox to safeguard astronauts and planetary habitats before ignition.
details:
What it does & how it works: PyroSage is an autonomous microgravity fire intelligence platform combining real-time 3D simulation with NASA combustion analysis. Its "Fiction Combustion" sandbox allows researchers to run pre-flight virtual experiments across five dynamic variables: gravity (0g microgravity, 0.17g Moon, 0.38g Mars, 1.0g Earth), oxygen concentration (15%–40%), cabin pressure (10–200 kPa), ventilation flow rate, and fuel material (PMMA polymer, cotton fabric, n-heptane droplets), calculating transport physics to render flame morphology, standoff thickness, and buoyant flow velocity. Its multimodal analysis pipeline ingests flame imagery, video frames, sensor CSV logs, and research documents, extracts geometric and spectral descriptors (symmetry IoU, defect depth, boundary roughness, centroid jitter), matches them against 77 registered combustion science techniques, and queries the NASA Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) repository (e.g., PSI-98 Saffire, PSI-107 FLEX, PSI-25 BASS-II) to generate printable safety reports.

Benefits: Enables zero-risk virtual modeling of hazardous, oxygen-enriched spacecraft cabin atmospheres without endangering crews or hardware. Detects low-temperature cool flames (600–1000 K) that persist via molecular diffusion after visible flames disappear. Eliminates weeks of manual comparison by automatically cross-referencing 36+ years of NASA spaceflight records. Features a resilient offline architecture with a deterministic physics fallback engine that guarantees continuous operation even if external cloud APIs disconnect.

Intended impact: Directly enhances astronaut safety aboard the ISS, Lunar Gateway, and long-duration Mars transit missions. Accelerates aerospace material certification by reducing the testing cycle and cost for space-grade polymers, flame retardants, and fabrics under the Artemis program. Democratizes microgravity research by giving universities, students, and global labs free, immediate access to physics-grounded space fire models without needing multi-million-dollar drop tower or orbital rocket flights.

Tools, languages & software: Python 3.12 backend with FastAPI and Uvicorn running serverless on Vercel Fluid Compute. Frontend built in vanilla JavaScript with zero framework overhead. Scientific processing using NumPy, SciPy, Pillow headless vision routines, and SQLite3. 3D visualization powered by a custom 5-layer raymarched Fractional Brownian Motion (fBM) volumetric flame shader running at 60 FPS in HTML5 Canvas. AI reasoning integrated via Google Gemini and OpenAI APIs guarded by deterministic physics validation. Document parsing via PyPDF, Python-Docx, OpenPyXL, and BeautifulSoup4. Continuous testing via GitHub Actions CI across Python 3.10, 3.11, and 3.12.

Creativity: Introduces "Fiction Combustion" to turn static combustion charts into intuitive, real-time parameter exploration where users directly manipulate fluid mechanics and chemical kinetics. Uses technique-bounded AI that strictly constrains interpretations to 77 numbered NASA methods and peer-reviewed flight data to prevent hallucinations. Integrates real-time 3D orbital controls, live telemetry HUD, audio narration, and printable documentation into a single unified workstation.

Key engineering factors: Accounted for the fundamental transition from Earth buoyant convection (Gr >> 1) to microgravity diffusion and Marangoni transport (Gr < 10^-4). Integrated partial-gravity atmospheric profiles for Lunar (0.16g–0.17g) and Martian (0.38g) habitats. Built for restricted serverless environments using read-only filesystem routing to /tmp and headless vision fallbacks to prevent C-library linking failures. Ensured all calculations, dimensionless numbers (Fr, Gr, Pe), and flight comparisons trace directly to verified NASA PSI datasets.
